viral_ticker_tweets.full_text_en:
Today I'm announcing Workers IO to solve the slowest part of engineering, verification!

AI agents can now write years’ worth of code in days, but it still takes significant engineering effort to verify what’s being built.

It’s impossible to predict all scenarios that could lead to a failure and that’s why most expensive failures are found in production.

Workers IO runs millions of simulated production scenarios on your entire system, including dependencies. These simulations run inside a deterministic hypervisor which injects faults like network delays, disk errors, clock skew, and process failures to verify how your system handles these conditions.

Deterministic execution allows us to systematically explore the state space of the system and perfectly reproduce failures.

We are already helping customers do years worth of production hardening in days and build confidence in what they’re shipping.

If you are working on systems that you can never afford to break, DM me and we can help you battle test them!
viral_ticker_tweets.full_text_zh:
今天我宣布 Workers IO 来解决工程中最慢的部分——验证！

人工智能代理现在可以在几天内编写出多年的代码，但仍然需要大量的工程工作来验证正在构建的内容。

不可能预测所有可能导致故障的情况，这就是为什么最昂贵的故障出现在生产中。

Workers IO 在整个系统上运行数百万个模拟生产场景，包括依赖项。这些模拟在确定性管理程序内运行，该管理程序会注入网络延迟、磁盘错误、时钟偏差和进程故障等故障，以验证系统如何处理这些条件。

确定性执行使我们能够系统地探索系统的状态空间并完美地重现故障。

我们已经帮助客户在几天内完成了长达数年的生产强化，并建立了对他们所运输产品的信心。

如果您正在开发无法承受损坏的系统，请私信我，我们可以帮助您对它们进行实际测试！

top_three.title: The New York Times sues Brave web browser for AI scraping and bypassing paywalls
top_three.title_en: The New York Times sues Brave web browser for AI scraping and bypassing paywalls
top_three.author: The Verge AI
top_three.content_snippet:
The New York Times and a group of other publications have filed lawsuits against the company that makes the Brave web browser over alleged unlawful scraping to train AI and also letting users bypass their paywalls, as reported by Reuters.

According to a complaint filed by the companies that run New York Daily News, the Chicago Tribune, and the Orlando Sentinel, Brave Software has monetized its index of scraped websites by, in part, providing AI companies with paid access to  "real-time online c
top_three.summary_en: Major media outlets, including The New York Times and The Chicago Tribune, have filed a lawsuit against Brave browser. The plaintiffs allege that Brave is illegally scraping content for its 'Brave Index' to sell to AI companies for model training and providing tools for users to bypass paywalls, violating copyright and business rights.
top_three.summary_zh: 纽约时报》等机构起诉Brave浏览器，指控其未经授权抓取数据用于AI训练并帮助用户绕过付费墙

【起因与机理】维护新闻内容商业版权，遏制AI公司未经授权的数据采集行为
【关键技术规格】多家知名媒体联手对峙Brave。
【观点态度】涉及AI训练数据合规性这一核心行业痛点。

[Root Cause & Mechanism] To protect commercial copyright and curb unauthorized AI data harvesting
[Key Specification] Major media publishers vs. Brave.
[Perspective & Impact] High-stakes battle over AI training data compliance.

top_three.title: OpenAI prepares lobbying blitz for a post-midterm Washington
top_three.title_en: OpenAI prepares lobbying blitz for a post-midterm Washington
top_three.author: THE DECODER
top_three.content_snippet:
OpenAI is gearing up for a political lobbying and PR push after the US midterms. According to Axios, the company is bracing for a tougher fight in Washington if Democrats win control of the House.

After two years under a friendly administration, big tech companies with close ties to President Trump are facing growing regulatory pressure. Rivals like Meta are already building bridges to Democrats. OpenAI's policy chief Chris Lehane plans to steer the AI debate through 2028 with a mix of new and
top_three.summary_en: OpenAI is ramping up lobbying efforts to navigate shifting political tides in Washington, promoting a narrative that AI won't replace humans while proposing 'speed limit' safety rules. The company is also rebranding energy-intensive data centers as 'AI Compute Campuses' to win public and regulatory support.

【起因与机理】应对大选后潜在的监管压力，确保公司在行业规则制定中的主导权
【关键技术规格】包装安全叙事与数据中心品牌。
【观点态度】意图通过立法锁定行业护城河。
fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] Chris Lehane, Head of Policy at OpenAI (Washington D.C. political circles): Launching lobbying blitz, proposing safety rules, and rebranding data centers

[Perspective & Impact] Attempting to lock in moats via legislation.

news.title: Goldman Sachs pulls AI coding tools from traders and bankers
news.title_en: Goldman Sachs pulls AI coding tools from traders and bankers
news.author: THE DECODER
news.content_snippet:
Goldman Sachs is pulling AI coding tools like Claude Code and GitHub Copilot from traders and bankers, limiting access to engineers only. As recently as July, CIO Marco Argenti publicly praised "vibe coding" by non-technical staff. Now the bank cites "productivity and risk management" as the reason for the reversal.

The article Goldman Sachs pulls AI coding tools from traders and bankers appeared first on The Decoder.
news.summary_en: Goldman Sachs has revoked access to AI coding tools like Claude Code and GitHub Copilot for traders and bankers, restricting usage to the engineering team. This marks a sharp pivot from the bank's previous support for 'vibe coding' by non-technical staff, citing productivity concerns and risk management.

news.title: Memo: Linux distribution vendor SUSE is laying off ~10% of its staff, saying "automation and AI are fundamentally shifting how software companies operate" (Liam Proven/The Register)

news.author: The Register
news.content_snippet:
One in ten employees at SUSE are facing the chop due to "automation and AI," according to a memo dispatched by management at the privately owned open source software biz.

In an email to the 1,900 strong workforce on Monday - seen by The Register - CEO Dirk-Peter van Leeuwen, the former Red Hat exec who joined SUSE in March 2023, confirmed the "difficult news."

"We are announcing a reduction of SUSE’s global workforce of approximately 10 percent," he said. "These decisions are painful for our p
news.summary_en: Open-source software company SUSE announced a global workforce reduction of approximately 10% in an internal memo from its CEO. This difficult decision was made after leadership scrutinized future strategies, driven by the belief that automation and AI are fundamentally shifting how software companies operate.

news.content_snippet:

news.summary_en: AI startup Anthropic has updated the system prompt for Claude Code to restrict users from recreating specific existing video games. news.title: Raising the quality of insights in agentic analytics

news.author: MIT Tech Review
news.content_snippet:
In just a few years, generative AI has changed the face of enterprise analytics, notably by making analytics accessible to users across the organization. Agentic AI promises to do even more, by automating entire workflows and taking actions based on agent insights. But there is a problem: The quality of insights that agents currently generate leaves much to be desired.

Fewer than half of agent-generated insights at the organizations surveyed for this report lead to business improvement. And whi

news.title: One brutal Minecraft night scared 50 AI agents into inventing chicken handoff protocols, a Fertilizer Officer, and fishing shifts
news.title_en: One brutal Minecraft night scared 50 AI agents into inventing chicken handoff protocols, a Fertilizer Officer, and fishing shifts
news.author: THE DECODER
news.content_snippet:
In experiments by Y Combinator Labs and Olam Labs, OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol model showed two very different sides. When 50 agents were tasked with peaceful civilization-building in Minecraft, they froze up in absurd bureaucracy. In direct competition against Claude Opus 5.5, they independently downloaded the game's source code to win. Simulations like these are meant to serve as an early warning system before AI swarms act unpredictably in real-world systems.

news.title: Stop counting tokens, start counting what ships
news.title_en: Stop counting tokens, start counting what ships
news.author: MIT Tech Review
news.summary_en:
When a developer gives an AI agent a coding task, the agent does more than answer once. It plans, generates code, runs tests, and repeats the process to correct errors. A single task can use 10 to 50 times more tokens than a basic chat prompt. The more useful the agent becomes, the more calls it makes. With per-token pricing, the workflows creating the most value can also become the most expensive.

The financial pressure is already visible. Uber reportedly exhausted its entire 2026 AI budget by

celebrity.full_text_en:
Today I'm announcing Workers IO to solve the slowest part of engineering, verification!

AI agents can now write years’ worth of code in days, but it still takes significant engineering effort to verify what’s being built.

It’s impossible to predict all scenarios that could lead to a failure and that’s why most expensive failures are found in production.

Workers IO runs millions of simulated production scenarios on your entire system, including dependencies. These simulations run inside a deterministic hypervisor which injects faults like network delays, disk errors, clock skew, and process failures to verify how your system handles these conditions.

Deterministic execution allows us to systematically explore the state space of the system and perfectly reproduce failures.

We are already helping customers do years worth of production hardening in days and build confidence in what they’re shipping.

If you are working on systems that you can never afford to break, DM me and we can help you battle test them!
celebrity.full_text_zh:
今天我宣布 Workers IO 来解决工程中最慢的部分——验证！

人工智能代理现在可以在几天内编写出多年的代码，但仍然需要大量的工程工作来验证正在构建的内容。

不可能预测所有可能导致故障的情况，这就是为什么最昂贵的故障出现在生产中。

Workers IO 在整个系统上运行数百万个模拟生产场景，包括依赖项。这些模拟在确定性管理程序内运行，该管理程序会注入网络延迟、磁盘错误、时钟偏差和进程故障等故障，以验证系统如何处理这些条件。

确定性执行使我们能够系统地探索系统的状态空间并完美地重现故障。

我们已经帮助客户在几天内完成了长达数年的生产强化，并建立了对他们所运输产品的信心。

如果您正在开发无法承受损坏的系统，请私信我，我们可以帮助您对它们进行实际测试！

celebrity.full_text_en:
Anything that holds money draws attackers who don't mind trying again.

I learned that the expensive way. I read on X that the Ostium vault I was in had been hacked, opened my wallet, and about $2,000 was gone.

AI agents with wallets have it worse, because the attacker only has to send them words. The trick has a name, prompt injection: an order slipped into ordinary text that the AI then follows.

In May 2026 one of those orders came disguised as Morse code, and around $200,000 left an agent's wallet.

As an engineer, I know a setup that stays the same every time will eventually show its weak spot to someone who keeps trying. That agent had one filter and one model, unchanged on every try.

@GenLayer's Greyboxing takes that sameness away. Its validators are the separate reviewers that run the network.

Before any AI reads your text, each one reworks it in its own hidden way, with its own model. What fools one of them looks like nonsense to everyone else, and the majority overrules any one that slips.

Every try now lands on a reader the attacker has never seen.

Would you let an AI agent hold your money today, or only once it works like this?

celebrity.full_text_en:
412 km up. 7.69 km/s. 3 engine bells, 4 landing legs, 8 hull sections that come apart in orbit and dock back together. meet the Halcyon HX-7, a new orbital freighter prototype that only exists as a simulator

I built it with Elvar's teardown method. one free Claude Code skill, the whole ship in one offline HTML page

the whole mission is one timeline. 9 phases: approach, hold, gear down, cargo open, mast up, optics scan, teardown, reassembly, ascent burn. every panel reads that timeline. the main drive sits at 86 kN on approach, drops to 13 kN while the hull is apart and climbs to 89 kN on the ascent burn. the moment the sections split, all 8 load bars flip to DETACHED. the gauges follow the model, so they can't show a number the ship isn't living through

here is the gist:

→ type /teardown, name the vehicle, attach one real reference. without it you get a toy
→ write the mission as a timeline before any part gets a shape: 9 phases, each with a start time
→ split the hull into sections you can pull out alone: drive, aft, mid, fwd, nose, pod, mast, gear
→ give every phase real numbers: thrust in kN, altitude, velocity, which subsystem is live
→ point every panel at the timeline, never at its own animation
→ blow the hull apart mid-mission and check that every bar says DETACHED
→ dock it back and fire the burn. if one section comes home late, the numbers show it before your eyes do

a ship you can open, cut and fly says more than a render deck

the 9 prompts are in the quoted article

nose iris opening in orbit or 4 legs coming down at 7.69 km/s, which part of your own ship would you cut open first?

↳ concept simulation, method from the article
celebrity.full_text_zh:
海拔412公里。 7.69 公里/秒。 3 个发动机罩、4 个着陆腿、8 个船体部分，它们在轨道上分开并重新对接在一起。认识 Halcyon HX-7，一种仅作为模拟器存在的新型轨道货机原型

我用 Elvar 的拆解方法构建了它。一项免费的 Claude Code 技能，整艘船都在一个离线 HTML 页面中

整个任务就是一条时间线。 9 个阶段：进场、等待、起落架放下、货物打开、桅杆升起、光学扫描、拆卸、重新组装、上升燃烧。每个小组都会阅读该时间表。主驱动装置在接近时为 86 kN，在船体分离时降至 13 kN，在上升燃烧时升至 89 kN。当部分分裂时，所有 8 个负载杆都会翻转为分离状态。仪表遵循模型，因此它们无法显示船舶未经历过的数字

要点如下：

→ 输入/teardown，为车辆命名，附上一份真实的参考资料。没有它你就会得到一个玩具
→ 在任何部分成型之前将任务写成时间线：9 个阶段，每个阶段都有一个开始时间
→ 将船体分成可单独拉出的部分：驱动部、船尾部、中部部、前部部、机头部、吊舱部、桅杆部、起落架部
→ 给出每个阶段的实数：推力（kN）、高度、速度、哪个子系统处于活动状态
→ 将每个面板指向时间轴，而不是其自己的动画
→ 在任务中将船体炸开并检查每个条是否都显示“分离”
→ 将其放回原位并点火。如果某个部分回家晚了，数字就会在你眼前显示出来

一艘可以打开、切割和飞行的船不仅仅意味着渲染甲板

celebrity.full_text_en:
My best friend said the sky would be clear. I trusted him so much I never checked.

He works at the weather station and does the daily report. I picked up the package and left without any other source.

Why would I? It's him. He does this every day.

Three hours later, I was stuck under Ikeja Bridge, the sky looking like a war zone. The package didn't make it.

He wasn't trying to fool me. He was just wrong, and I had no second source to catch it.

Now imagine someone who was trying.

In May, a tweet hid a transfer order in Morse code. Grok decoded it, Bankrbot took the result as a command, and around $200,000 moved. That's prompt injection: an instruction smuggled into something the AI was only meant to read.

One model and one filter meant one thing to study. An attacker could rehearse on it until the trick worked.

@GenLayer's Greyboxing is the second source I skipped. Before any model sees your text, every validator rewrites it with secret defenses, then runs its own model. A trick that fools one has to fool every other model too, against defenses it can't see. And a validator that still bites gets outvoted.

I skipped the cross-check once and lost a package. An agent with a wallet loses a lot more.

What's one thing you'd never let an AI agent do for you without a second source, and why?
celebrity.full_text_zh:
我最好的朋友说天空会晴朗。我非常信任他，所以从来没有检查过。

他在气象站工作并制作每日报告。我拿起包裹就离开了，没有任何其他来源。

我为什么要这么做？是他。他每天都这样做。

三小时后，我被困在伊凯贾桥下，天空看起来像战区。包裹没有成功。

他并不是想愚弄我。他错了，而我没有第二个来源可以捕捉到这一点。

现在想象一下有人正在尝试。

五月份，一条推文隐藏了一份摩尔斯电码转账指令。 Grok 对其进行了解码，Bankrbot 将结果作为命令，大约 20 万美元被转移。这就是即时注入：一条指令被偷偷地植入人工智能只能读取的内容中。

一个模型和一个滤波器意味着研究一件事。攻击者可以对其进行排练，直到该技巧起作用为止。

@GenLayer 的 Greyboxing 是我跳过的第二个来源。在任何模型看到您的文本之前，每个验证器都会使用秘密防御重写它，然后运行自己的模型。一个欺骗一个人的技巧也必须欺骗所有其他模型，以对抗它看不到的防御。仍然有效的验证者会被否决。

我有一次跳过了交叉检查并丢失了一个包裹。一个有钱包的经纪人损失更多。

在没有第二来源的情况下，你永远不会让人工智能代理为你做的一件事是什么？为什么？

celebrity.title_zh:
专业化可以使人工智能代理在特定任务上表现得异常出色，但当情况发生变化时，它也可能会暴露出其弱点。

这是 @agentdojo 需要考虑的有用维度。当代理人在共享条件下竞争时，他们的不同设计可以揭示策略是否真正具有适应性或只是针对少数情况进
celebrity.full_text_en:
specialisation can make an AI agent exceptionally good at a particular task, but it can also expose its weaknesses when the situation changes.

That is a useful dimension to consider with @agentdojo . When agents compete under shared conditions,their different designs can reveal whether a strategy is genuinely adaptable or simply optimised for a narrow set of circumstances.

For builders,that insight goes beyond winning a match. It can help expose where an agent’s design needs improvement before the same weakness appears in a real deployment.

Powered by @rarelistio
celebrity.full_text_zh:
专业化可以使人工智能代理在特定任务上表现得异常出色，但当情况发生变化时，它也可能会暴露出其弱点。

这是 @agentdojo 需要考虑的有用维度。当代理人在共享条件下竞争时，他们的不同设计可以揭示策略是否真正具有适应性或只是针对少数情况进行优化。

对于建设者来说，这种洞察力不仅仅是赢得一场比赛。它可以帮助在实际部署中出现相同的弱点之前揭示代理的设计需要改进的地方。

prompts.title_en: Production-Grade Fullstack .cursorrules Template for Cursor & Windsurf
prompts.scenario: 💻 编程研发 / 自动化规范
prompts.takeaway_zh: 杜绝 AI 盲目重构全量文件、使用已弃用 API 或编造虚假第三方依赖包，强制执行防御性编程与自动化单测补全。
prompts.takeaway_en: Prevents AI from hallucinating npm packages, breaking documentation, or re-writing entire files. Enforces defensive coding and unit tests.
prompts.code_snippet:
# Cursor & Windsurf Project Rules (.cursorrules)

## 1. Documentation & Code Integrity
- Maintain documentation integrity: Never strip or alter unrelated existing docstrings and comments.
- Preserving context: When modifying a function, preserve surrounding logic and existing edge-case handlers.
- Targeted replacements: Always make minimal surgical edits instead of replacing entire file contents.

## 2. Dependency & API Safety
- Strictly forbid hallucinating npm/pip packages. Only import dependencies already declared in package.json / requirements.txt.
- Verify API signatures before calling external methods. Prefer standard library solutions where feasible.

## 3. Architecture & Type Safety
- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.
- Defensive coding: Always validate external inputs and handle potential null/undefined values gracefully.

## 4. Testing & Verification Gate
- Every new core feature or bugfix must be accompanied by corresponding unit tests.
- Never declare a task complete without executing lint checks and unit tests in terminal.
prompts.usage_guide_zh: 将以上配置代码复制并保存到项目根目录下的 `.cursorrules` 文件中，Cursor 与 Windsurf 在每次生成代码和执行 Agent 任务时均会自动以此规范为最高准则约束输出。
prompts.usage_guide_en: Copy and save the above rules into `.cursorrules` in your project root directory. Cursor & Windsurf will automatically enforce these guidelines during agent coding.

结构要求：
1. 【0-3秒冷开钩子】：第一帧必须有视觉颠覆或动作冲突（{{第1秒颠覆钩子}}），直接打破常规，禁止废话铺垫；

prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡级别的高级商业数据分析师，精通结构化因果归因与杜邦拆解分析。

针对我提供的 {{业务指标}} 数据，其近期出现 {{异常表现}}，请按以下框架深度剖析：
1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；
2. 【多维下钻 (Drill-down)】：从 {{维度拆解}}（如渠道、地域、品类、新老客）分析异常聚集点；
3. 【可执行建议】：摒弃假大空的套话，给出接下来 48 小时内的 3 个立竿见影的动作与 1 个监控预警公式。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior business intelligence analyst. Dissect the metric anomaly into component drivers, perform multi-dimensional drill-down, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation steps.

【杜邦拆解贡献率分析】：
1. 渠道维度：自然搜索量稳定（波动 <2%），但付费投流渠道跳出率贡献了 72% 的下跌额度；
2. 终端维度：移动端 iOS 表现正常，Android Web 呈现断崖式报错，核心原因是新版本结账 SDK 在低内存机型发生闪退。

【48小时纠偏行动】：
- 动作1 (技术)：立即灰度回滚 Android 渠道结账前端包至 v2.4.1；
- 动作2 (运营)：向受影响但未支付成功的 1,420 位加购用户推送 5 元免门槛补偿券唤醒；
- 动作3 (预警)：在 Grafana 建立警报公式：`IF(Cart_to_Checkout_Ratio < 0.65, Alert_P0, Normal)`。

"""

viral_posts.summary_en:
Today I'm announcing Workers IO to solve the slowest part of engineering, verification!

AI agents can now write years’ worth of code in days, but it still takes significant engineering effort to verify what’s being built.

It’s impossible to predict all scenarios that could lead to a failure and that’s why most expensive failures are found in production.

Workers IO runs millions of simulated production scenarios on your entire system, including dependencies. These simulations run inside a deterministic hypervisor which injects faults like network delays, disk errors, clock skew, and process failures to verify how your system handles these conditions.

Deterministic execution allows us to systematically explore the state space of the system and perfectly reproduce failures.

We are already helping customers do years worth of production hardening in days and build confidence in what they’re shipping.

If you are working on systems that you can never afford to break, DM me and we can help you battle test them!

viral_posts.title_en:
Anything that holds money draws attackers who don't mind trying again.

I learned that the expensive way. I read on X that the Ostium vault I was in had been hacked, opened my wallet, and about $2,000 was gone.

AI agents with wallets have it worse, because the attacker only has to send them words. The trick has a name, prompt injection: an order slipped into ordinary text that the AI then follows.

In May 2026 one of those orders came disguised as Morse code, and around $200,000 left an agent's wallet.

As an engineer, I know a setup that stays the same every time will eventually show its weak spot to someone who keeps trying. That agent had one filter and one model, unchanged on every try.

@GenLayer's Greyboxing takes that sameness away. Its validators are the separate reviewers that run the network.

Before any AI reads your text, each one reworks it in its own hidden way, with its own model. What fools one of them looks like nonsense to everyone else, and the majority overrules any one that slips.

Every try now lands on a reader the attacker has never seen.

Would you let an AI agent hold your money today, or only once it works like this?

viral_posts.title_en:
412 km up. 7.69 km/s. 3 engine bells, 4 landing legs, 8 hull sections that come apart in orbit and dock back together. meet the Halcyon HX-7, a new orbital freighter prototype that only exists as a simulator

I built it with Elvar's teardown method. one free Claude Code skill, the whole ship in one offline HTML page

the whole mission is one timeline. 9 phases: approach, hold, gear down, cargo open, mast up, optics scan, teardown, reassembly, ascent burn. every panel reads that timeline. the main drive sits at 86 kN on approach, drops to 13 kN while the hull is apart and climbs to 89 kN on the ascent burn. the moment the sections split, all 8 load bars flip to DETACHED. the gauges follow the model, so they can't show a number the ship isn't living through

here is the gist:

→ type /teardown, name the vehicle, attach one real reference. without it you get a toy
→ write the mission as a timeline before any part gets a shape: 9 phases, each with a start time
→ split the hull into sections you can pull out alone: drive, aft, mid, fwd, nose, pod, mast, gear
→ give every phase real numbers: thrust in kN, altitude, velocity, which subsystem is live
→ point every panel at the timeline, never at its own animation
→ blow the hull apart mid-mission and check that every bar says DETACHED
→ dock it back and fire the burn. if one section comes home late, the numbers show it before your eyes do

a ship you can open, cut and fly says more than a render deck

the 9 prompts are in the quoted article

海拔412公里。 7.69 公里/秒。 3 个发动机罩、4 个着陆腿、8 个船体部分，它们在轨道上分开并重新对接在一起。认识 Halcyon HX-7，一种仅作为模拟器存在的新型轨道货机原型

我用 Elvar 的拆解方法构建了它。一项免费的 Claude Code 技能，整艘船都在一个离线 HTML 页面中

整个任务就是一条时间线。 9 个阶段：进场、等待、起落架放下、货物打开、桅杆升起、光学扫描、拆卸、重新组装、上升燃烧。每个小组都会阅读该时间表。主驱动装置在接近时为 86 kN，在船体分离时降至 13 kN，在上升燃烧时升至 89 kN。当部分分裂时，所有 8 个负载杆都会翻转为分离状态。仪表遵循模型，因此它们无法显示船舶未经历过的数字

要点如下：

→ 输入/teardown，为车辆命名，附上一份真实的参考资料。没有它你就会得到一个玩具
→ 在任何部分成型之前将任务写成时间线：9 个阶段，每个阶段都有一个开始时间
→ 将船体分成可单独拉出的部分：驱动部、船尾部、中部部、前部部、机头部、吊舱部、桅杆部、起落架部
→ 给出每个阶段的实数：推力（kN）、高度、速度、哪个子系统处于活动状态
→ 将每个面板指向时间轴，而不是其自己的动画
→ 在任务中将船体炸开并检查每个条是否都显示“分离”
→ 将其放回原位并点火。如果某个部分回家晚了，数字就会在你眼前显示出来

一艘可以打开、切割和飞行的船不仅仅意味着渲染甲板

viral_posts.title_en:
My best friend said the sky would be clear. I trusted him so much I never checked.

He works at the weather station and does the daily report. I picked up the package and left without any other source.

Why would I? It's him. He does this every day.

Three hours later, I was stuck under Ikeja Bridge, the sky looking like a war zone. The package didn't make it.

He wasn't trying to fool me. He was just wrong, and I had no second source to catch it.

Now imagine someone who was trying.

In May, a tweet hid a transfer order in Morse code. Grok decoded it, Bankrbot took the result as a command, and around $200,000 moved. That's prompt injection: an instruction smuggled into something the AI was only meant to read.

One model and one filter meant one thing to study. An attacker could rehearse on it until the trick worked.

@GenLayer's Greyboxing is the second source I skipped. Before any model sees your text, every validator rewrites it with secret defenses, then runs its own model. A trick that fools one has to fool every other model too, against defenses it can't see. And a validator that still bites gets outvoted.

I skipped the cross-check once and lost a package. An agent with a wallet loses a lot more.

What's one thing you'd never let an AI agent do for you without a second source, and why?

三小时后，我被困在伊凯贾桥下，天空看起来像战区。包裹没有成功。

他并不是想愚弄我。他错了，而我没有第二个来源可以捕捉到这一点。

现在想象一下有人正在尝试。

五月份，一条推文隐藏了一份摩尔斯电码转账指令。 Grok 对其进行了解码，Bankrbot 将结果作为命令，大约 20 万美元被转移。这就是即时注入：一条指令被偷偷地植入人工智能只能读取的内容中。

一个模型和一个滤波器意味着研究一件事。攻击者可以对其进行排练，直到该技巧起作用为止。

@GenLayer 的 Greyboxing 是我跳过的第二个来源。在任何模型看到您的文本之前，每个验证器都会使用秘密防御重写它，然后运行自己的模型。一个欺骗一个人的技巧也必须欺骗所有其他模型，以对抗它看不到的防御。仍然有效的验证者会被否决。

我有一次跳过了交叉检查并丢失了一个包裹。一个有钱包的经纪人损失更多。

在没有第二来源的情况下，你永远不会让人工智能代理为你做的一件事是什么？为什么？

viral_posts.summary_en:
My best friend said the sky would be clear. I trusted him so much I never checked.

He works at the weather station and does the daily report. I picked up the package and left without any other source.

Why would I? It's him. He does this every day.

Three hours later, I was stuck under Ikeja Bridge, the sky looking like a war zone. The package didn't make it.

He wasn't trying to fool me. He was just wrong, and I had no second source to catch it.

Now imagine someone who was trying.

In May, a tweet hid a transfer order in Morse code. Grok decoded it, Bankrbot took the result as a command, and around $200,000 moved. That's prompt injection: an instruction smuggled into something the AI was only meant to read.

One model and one filter meant one thing to study. An attacker could rehearse on it until the trick worked.

@GenLayer's Greyboxing is the second source I skipped. Before any model sees your text, every validator rewrites it with secret defenses, then runs its own model. A trick that fools one has to fool every other model too, against defenses it can't see. And a validator that still bites gets outvoted.

I skipped the cross-check once and lost a package. An agent with a wallet loses a lot more.

What's one thing you'd never let an AI agent do for you without a second source, and why?

viral_posts.title_en:
Imagine a customer telling your AI agent "yeah, sure" in the most frustrated tone possible.

The transcript looks perfectly normal, but anyone listening can tell something is wrong.

And that's the problem with voice AI today. Understanding the words isn't enough if you can't understand how they're being said.

Pretty interesting approach from @hume_ai.
viral_posts.title_zh:
想象一下，一位客户以最沮丧的语气告诉你的人工智能代理“是的，当然”。

文字记录看起来完全正常，但任何人听都可以看出有什么问题。

这就是当今语音人工智能的问题。如果您无法理解这些词是如何表达的，那么仅仅理解这些词是不够的。

@hume_
